clue.text: Agreement resulting from investing millions in firm commitment

indicators.note: investing one thing in another puts it inside, so the abbreviation for millions goes into the run of letters for firm and commitment

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company, a firm
a promise is a commitment to do something
M is the standard abbreviation for million(s)

explanation.surface: A deal reached after millions are poured into a company's firm pledge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'firm commitment' reads as a single phrase, a binding pledge, but it splits into two pieces, and 'investing' puts the millions between them.
explanation.definitionFit: A settlement in which each side gives ground is an agreement reached by mutual concession.

clue.text: A source of food in church outlet

indicators.note: in places the first pieces inside the letters for church

parts.note: CE is the Church of England

indicators.note: the source of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A place in a church where food is served, such as a parish tearoom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A source of food' looks like the definition, but it is wordplay: A plus F inside CE.
explanation.definitionFit: A coffee shop is a retail outlet, a premises selling food and drink to the public.

clue.text: This may be over the pecking order

definitions.text: This may be over the pecking order

parts.words: This may be over the pecking order
parts.note: the plant hung over a doorway at Christmas, under which people kiss (peck); 'pecking order' suggests a hierarchy of birds

explanation.surface: Something that sits above a flock's hierarchy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pecking order' suggests rank among hens; here pecking means kissing, and the plant hangs over those who kiss beneath it.
explanation.definitionFit: The festive sprig hung above doorways invites anyone standing under it to be kissed.

clue.text: Show where Shakespeare's lover has a change of heart

indicators.note: the middle letter of the name is swapped for a different one, a new heart

parts.note: Romeo is the lover in Shakespeare's Romeo and Juliet

explanation.surface: A play in which Shakespeare's romantic hero changes his mind.
explanation.walkthrough: The central M of ROMEO is replaced by D.
explanation.definitionFit: A cowboy contest of riding and roping is a public show or exhibition.

clue.text: Borders of world full of spirit

indicators.note: a container full of something holds it inside, so the planet's letters wrap round the drink

parts.note: Mars is a world, a planet
gin is a spirit

explanation.surface: The edges of a world brimming with some vital force.
explanation.definitionFit: Edges of a page or region are its borders, the strips along the outside.

clue.text: Sticks up broken leg to avoid customs duty

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: gums means sticks with glue

indicators.note: broken means the letters are knocked out of order

explanation.surface: Someone with a broken leg on crutches somehow dodges paying import tax.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns GUMS into SMUG; 'broken' gives GLE from LEG.
explanation.definitionFit: To bring goods in secretly is to dodge the import tax that would be charged on them.

clue.text: Red Dwarf's leading actor?

definitions.meaning: a red dwarf is a small cool sun-like body in astronomy
the headline performer in a show or film

explanation.walkthrough: Red Dwarf is also a British TV sitcom, which makes 'leading actor' look like a question about its cast.
explanation.definitionFit: A red dwarf is a type of celestial sun, and the top-billed performer is called the same.

clue.text: Attempted promoting one, feeling exhausted

indicators.note: promoting raises something; in a down entry the letter for one moves up a place

parts.note: tried means attempted
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone who tried for a promotion now feels worn out.
explanation.walkthrough: TRIED becomes TIRED when the I moves up one place.
explanation.definitionFit: Being worn out means feeling weary, drained of energy.

clue.text: They say bank has assimilated troubled red-top

indicators.note: assimilating takes something in, so the word for bank holds the scrambled letters

parts.note: to bank on is to rely on

indicators.note: troubled means disturbed, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A tabloid in difficulty has been absorbed by a bank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'troubled' gives PORTED from REDTOP; a red-top is a British tabloid newspaper, named for its red masthead.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying something is so according to rumour or accounts is what 'they say' expresses.

clue.text: Perfectionist must see agreement is in Italian

indicators.note: in places the words for agreement and is inside the abbreviation for Italian

parts.note: IT is short for Italian, as in gin and it (Italian vermouth)
a deal is an agreement

explanation.surface: A perfectionist insists on an Italian contract.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who pursues flawless standards is a dreamer of how things ought to be, an idealist.

clue.text: United force American-English defender at the outset

parts.note: F is the physics symbol for force
US means American

indicators.note: the outset is the start, so only the first letter is taken

explanation.surface: A football team's force with an English-born American defender at kick-off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'United' looks like a football club name; here it means joined.
explanation.definitionFit: Things melted or welded together are joined into one, so they are united.

clue.text: Journey made for a game of golf?

definitions.text: Journey made for a game of golf?

parts.words: Journey made for a game of golf?
parts.note: a game of golf is a round, so a trip made for one is jokingly a there-and-back journey

explanation.walkthrough: A game of golf is a round, so a trip for one is a round trip, which really means a journey there and back.
explanation.definitionFit: An outward and return journey to the same starting point is a there-and-back excursion.

clue.text: Baffling call on feminine facilities

indicators.note: in an across entry, on means placed after the earlier letters

parts.note: facilities is a euphemism for toilets, and loo is British slang for a toilet
to ring is to call on the telephone

explanation.surface: A puzzling phone call about women's toilets.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that knocks you down metaphorically leaves you stumped, so it is baffling.

clue.text: Tree nearly everybody gets embarrassed about

indicators.note: nearly means the word is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: all means everybody

indicators.note: about means turned round, read backwards

parts.note: red means blushing, embarrassed

explanation.surface: Nearly everyone blushes at a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nearly' turns ALL into AL; 'about' turns RED into DER.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a birch-family tree common near water, so it is an example of a tree.

clue.text: Putting vessel inside oven like this is a bloomer

indicators.note: putting one thing inside another places it within the other's letters

parts.note: an Aga is a British range cooker, an oven
thus means in this way, like this
a pan is a cooking vessel

explanation.surface: A kitchen instruction to put a dish in the oven, which turns out to be a gaffe.
explanation.walkthrough: An AGA is a heavy cast-iron range cooker found in many British country kitchens. 'Bloomer' looks like a blunder but means a flowering plant.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the African lily, a flowering plant, so it is a bloomer in the sense of a flower.

clue.text: Understands and gets together

definitions.meaning: infers or grasps, as in 'I take it that'

explanation.definitionFit: To infer is one sense of the word, and to collect or assemble is the other.

clue.text: Still supporting European Commission over the moon

indicators.note: in a down entry, supporting means lying underneath the other part

parts.note: static means still, not moving

explanation.surface: A motionless figure backing the European Commission is delighted.
explanation.definitionFit: Over the moon is a British idiom for delighted, thrilled.

clue.text: Gourmet pie cooked with salt

indicators.note: cooked suggests the letters are worked over into a new arrangement

parts.note: to salt meat is to cure it

explanation.surface: A food lover's pie made with salt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooked' turns PIE into EPI.
explanation.definitionFit: A person with refined taste in food and drink is a connoisseur of fine dining.

clue.text: A Parisian told it's beside the point

parts.note: un is French for a, as a Parisian would say it
related means told, recounted

explanation.surface: Something a Parisian said is irrelevant.
explanation.definitionFit: Something with no connection to the matter in hand is irrelevant, beside the point.

clue.text: Happy to find rental contract, occupying vacant pad

indicators.note: occupying means living inside, so the contract word goes within the other letters
vacant means emptied of its middle, leaving the outer letters

parts.note: a lease is a rental contract

explanation.surface: Delighted to find a tenancy agreement for an empty flat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vacant pad' gives PD; pad is slang for a flat.
explanation.definitionFit: Being glad or content is a synonym for being happy.

clue.text: Please place a bet for a grand-looking old lady

parts.note: do is used as a polite request, as in 'do sit down', so it stands for please
to wager is to place a bet

explanation.surface: A request to put money on a bet for an elderly lady.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Please place a bet' reads as 'do wager'.
explanation.definitionFit: A widow holding a title from her late husband is typically a stately elderly woman.

clue.text: Genuine person who's the obvious choice

definitions.meaning: someone ideally suited, as in 'she's a ___ for the role'

explanation.definitionFit: The word means real or unaffected, and also someone born for a role.

clue.text: Country fair e.g. intended to keep going north

indicators.note: in a down entry, going north means the letters are read upwards, backwards
the words keep the letters within them, concealing them

explanation.surface: A country fair, for example, that was meant to keep moving north.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run backwards through 'fAIR EG INtended'.
explanation.definitionFit: This West African state is a nation, Africa's most populous.

clue.text: This girl may provide average answer!

parts.note: the norm is the average, the usual standard

explanation.surface: A girl who may give an ordinary reply.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a female first name, so it fits a girl.

clue.text: Rustic wall painting showing river for miles

indicators.note: the letter for river replaces the letter for miles

parts.note: a mural is a wall painting

explanation.surface: A country-style mural depicting a river stretching for miles.
explanation.walkthrough: R (river) replaces M (miles) in MURAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean belonging to the countryside, simple and country-like.

clue.text: Wit upsetting A-list fliers

parts.note: a wag is a witty person

indicators.note: upsetting overturns the order of the letters

explanation.surface: A joker offends the celebrity elite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upsetting' turns ALIST into TAILS.
explanation.definitionFit: These are small long-tailed songbirds, so they are birds, creatures that fly.

clue.text: Fruit pile oddly eaten by primate

indicators.note: something eaten by another goes inside it

parts.note: an ape is a primate

indicators.note: oddly takes the first, third and other odd-placed letters

explanation.surface: A heap of fruit wolfed down by a monkey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly' takes PL from 'pile'.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a common orchard produce, an example of fruit.

clue.text: Dish offered by side finishing early

indicators.note: finishing early means the word stops before its last letter

parts.note: a flank is a side

explanation.surface: A dish brought by a team that finished its match early.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finishing early' turns FLANK into FLAN.
explanation.definitionFit: An open pastry tart is a dish, savoury or sweet.

clue.text: Warning sign from mostly tough heavy drinker

indicators.note: mostly means all but the last letter is kept

parts.note: hard means tough
a binger drinks heavily in bouts

explanation.surface: An alarm signal coming from a hardened boozer.
explanation.definitionFit: A forerunner or omen announcing what is coming acts as a warning sign.

clue.text: A bit of flower power — and others

parts.note: P is the physics symbol for power
et al is Latin shorthand for 'and others'

explanation.surface: Flower power, the hippie slogan, and its followers.
explanation.definitionFit: Each coloured leaf of a bloom is one segment of the flower.

clue.text: Second kind person given briefs?

parts.note: ilk means kind or type

explanation.surface: Another kindly person gets handed underwear.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a senior barrister (King's Counsel) is called this, after the gown; barristers are given briefs (cases).
explanation.definitionFit: A senior barrister in Britain receives briefs, the instructions for a case.

clue.text: A room with old academic is a battle

parts.note: aged means old
a don is a university academic

explanation.surface: A room shared with an elderly professor turns into a fight.
explanation.definitionFit: The final apocalyptic conflict in the Bible is the archetypal great battle.
